headline: Executive order sets limits on when federal agencies can pay contingency fees, such as to private lawyers hired to represent the government.
what_it_does: Based on its title, this order sets rules meant to keep federal agencies from paying contingency fees, which are fees based on a share of money won or recovered. Such fees are common when private lawyers are hired to handle cases. No summary was provided, so the exact rules, limits, and exceptions are not described here.

who_it_affects.how: They likely face new rules or limits on hiring outside help that is paid through contingency fees.

who_it_affects.group: Private lawyers and firms that work for the federal government
who_it_affects.how: They may face limits on being paid a share of the money they win or recover for the government.

when_it_takes_effect: Signed May 16, 2007; the effective date is not stated in the provided material.
